about: The thin line's twelve operations as the old blueprint records them. Extracted, not designed: every value is read from the files named under `source`. It is the input for roadmap step 1.1.

perOperation: ret: a success prints exactly the returns schema with --json
ref (one per refusal): from <starting world>, it refuses with <error>, its exit code and shape, and changes nothing
evt (one per event): it sends <event>, valid against its schema, carrying trace_id
spn: one trace from the CLI command through the SDK to the server, with every declared span
bud: end to end, p95 ≤ <p95> ms and p50 ≤ <p50> ms over N warm runs

sharedDoubts: The old error codes are one shared list of upper-case codes, each with a CLI exit code (`blueprint/shared/vocabulary.ts`). The spike contract declares a typed refusal per operation with its own fields (`DuplicateEntry { key }` in `spikes/pipeline/contract/record.ts`). The old records do not say which fields a refusal carries: only some examples show a `details` object.

The old events are state-change events (`<thing>_transitioned` with `from`, `to`, `transition` and ids). The spike contract says a successful call emits each declared event exactly once, and that what it carries is a pure function of the payload and the result (`spikes/pipeline/contract/operation.ts`). Several old events carry values that are in neither (for example `epoch`, `kind`, `person_id`, `nonce`), and several are sent only on one branch of the operation.

Every refusal names a starting world (`given`). In the old blueprint these are named snapshots built by a local supervisor's builder script (`blueprint/devnet/worlds.ts`). The roadmap makes a world an Alchemy deployment with a Neon branch, and step 0.9 speaks of a template world. Five of the 20 starting worlds the twelve name are not in the old catalog at all (see the list near the end).

The old records speak of two places a world runs: a local devnet on one machine ("anyone on the machine") and a hosted service. Roadmap rule 5 says a world never lives on the agent's own machine, and the roadmap names three grades (private, shared, real) where the old `kind` is local, simulated, staging or production.

The twelve steps do not include the operations that make their own starting state: signing in, claiming a personal Safe, inviting and seating a member, seating a second Director, approving a proposal. `evals/thin-line.md` says the run starts from an empty world.
`CLI_USAGE` is listed as a refusal or an error of every one of the twelve. It is a fault of the command line, raised by the CLI before any call reaches the door.
The old budgets are a pair (p50, p95) per class, measured end to end at the CLI (`packages/blueprint-engine/src/budgets.ts`). The spike contract holds one number, `budgetMs`, measured on the server.

The door's operations (`doc.*`, `report.*`) and `org.member.grant` do not say how the world is named on the command line. `evals/thin-line.md` says to keep the world id in every command. Only the `world ...` and `record ...` commands take a world, and `org create` by a decision that no record carries out.

orderByWhatTheyTouch.rule: Fewest always-needed parts first; equal counts keep the journey's order. A part counts when the operation's own call needs it. What only the thin line's claim needs is under `touches` of each operation. An operation early in this order can still need state that only a later one makes; the last column says what.

list.needsFirst: A world with a record. For the claim's lineage: a world restored from another.
A world. For the claim: a world restored from another.
A company with a ready site, and a caller whose Frappe user a hat created (so hats must have reached the site first).

sometimesNeeds: clock: only for the claim: the balance is read "at the world's now"
list.needsFirst: A company with a ready site, a caller with a site user, and for the claim a posted payment.

sometimesNeeds: Frappe site: only with `--profile full` and a template that has companies
snapshot store: only with a `--template` saved from a snapshot

events.about: A world changed state: began creating, started, stopped, resumed, began restoring, finished restoring, was parked for being idle or closed. Carries the world id, its kind, the new state and the epoch; never a company, an address or a key.
events.properties: { from: "creating" | "running" | "stopped" | "restoring" | "parked" | "closed" | null, to: "creating" | "running" | "stopped" | "restoring" | "parked" | "closed", transition: "create" | "start" | "stop" | "resume" | "restore" | "restored" | "park" | "close", world_id: string, kind: "local" | "simulated" | "staging" | "production", epoch: number }

events.about: An Organization's setup changed state: begun, waiting for the founder's authorization, back to processing, ready, needing attention, resumed or failed. Replaces organization_creation_started, _ready and _failed.
events.properties: { from: string | null, to: string, transition: string, org_id: string, person_id: string, issue_reason: string | null }

events.about: An app was added to an Organization (installed native at birth, or wanted), installed on its head, removed or wanted again. The head connection's process installs a wanted app from it.
events.properties: { from: string | null, to: string, transition: string, org_id: string, app: string, native: boolean }

events.about: A Party changed state: it was named, onboarded, claimed, registered, activated or released. `from` is null at a birth. `owner_kind` and `owner_id` are the Party's tenant once it has one. It never carries a mailbox, a handle or a name.
events.properties: { from: "provisional" | "outside" | "pending" | "active" | "released" | null, to: "provisional" | "outside" | "pending" | "active" | "released", transition: "name_person" | "name_address" | "adopt_mailbox" | "onboard" | "claim" | "register" | "activate" | "release", party_id: string, kind: "person" | "agent" | "organization" | "address", owner_kind: "person" | "organization" | null, owner_id: string | null }

events.about: An officer hat change changed state: proposed, applied or ended. It names the permission and the proposal, never the member or the note; the proposing Director is the envelope's actor. Notices tells the member from it.
events.properties: { from: "proposed" | "applied" | "ended" | null, to: "proposed" | "applied" | "ended", transition: "propose" | "apply" | "end", change_id: string, org_id: string, change: "grant" | "revoke", permission: "manage-books" | "issue-invoices" | "manage-people", proposal_id: string }

events.about: A Board proposal changed state. Every opener's workflow follows it by its subject (the opener, kind and id are on it), notices tells the Directors a proposal waits for them, and the funnel reads it; `from` is null at birth. The runtime writes it to the outbox in the transition's transaction.
events.properties: { from: "awaiting_approvals" | "executed" | "failed" | "rejected" | "replaced" | null, to: "awaiting_approvals" | "executed" | "failed" | "rejected" | "replaced", transition: "propose" | "execute" | "fail" | "reject" | "replace", proposal_id: string, org_id: string, kind: "transaction" | "rejection" | "scheduled_payment", nonce: integer, opener: "board" | "agents" | "budgets" | "payments" | "payroll" | "equity", subject_kind: string, subject_id: string }

events.about: An approval changed state. Its opener's workflows are triggered by it (the opener's subject is on it) and the funnel reads it; `from` is null at birth. The runtime writes it to the outbox in the transition's transaction.
events.properties: { from: "sponsoring" | "pending" | "signed" | "sending" | "sent" | "landed" | "reverted" | "displaced" | "expired" | "declined" | "refused" | "withdrawn" | null, to: "sponsoring" | "pending" | "signed" | "sending" | "sent" | "landed" | "reverted" | "displaced" | "expired" | "declined" | "refused" | "withdrawn", transition: "open" | "sponsor" | "refuse" | "sign" | "decline" | "withdraw" | "claim_send" | "accept" | "bounce" | "land" | "revert" | "displace" | "expire", approval_id: string, person_id: string, org_id: string | null, opener: "accounts" | "organizations" | "board" | "agents" | "budgets" | "payments" | "payroll" | "equity", subject_kind: string, subject_id: string }

events.about: A payment held for a Frappe document changed state: prepared (waiting for a signature), sent (the chain confirmed it), failed (refused or reverted), hash mismatch (the draft changed after it was prepared), abandoned (the person cancelled the draft) or reversed (a paid document was cancelled, so money came back by a new payment). Carries the Organization, the request, the doctype and the new state; never the amount, the party or the address. The 'pay an invoice from Frappe' funnel reads it.
events.properties: { from: "waiting" | "sent" | "failed" | "mismatch" | "abandoned" | "reversed" | null, to: "waiting" | "sent" | "failed" | "mismatch" | "abandoned" | "reversed", transition: "prepare" | "land" | "fail" | "mismatch" | "abandon" | "reverse", org_id: string, request_id: string, doctype: string }

events.about: A Payment changed state. Requests (paid), banking (a payout's Payment), notices and activity follow it through the outbox. `outcome` says why a Payment lapsed or was cancelled.
events.properties: { from: "prepared" | "scheduled" | "due" | "escrowed" | "submitted" | "needs_retry" | "settled" | "mismatched" | "cancelled" | null, to: "prepared" | "scheduled" | "due" | "escrowed" | "submitted" | "needs_retry" | "settled" | "mismatched" | "cancelled", transition: string, payment_id: string, owner_kind: "person" | "organization", owner_id: string, command_id: string | null, route: "personal" | "budget" | "board" | "claim_escrow" | "chain", outcome: "declined" | "refused" | "rejected" | "expired" | "displaced" | "reverted" | "window_closed" | "voided" | "budget_cancelled" | "refunded" | "withdrawn" | null }
